request.notes: `task_type` is one of task/epic/gate and is ALWAYS sent even when it equals the upstream default, the same discipline the read side applies to `with_claims`. A `gate` requires `metadata.gate_type` in human/timer/ci/pr/external_task, and a `timer` gate additionally a parseable `metadata.ready_at`. `metadata` must NOT carry `depends_on`/`blocked_on` — dependencies are first-class edges, passed as `depends_on`, each of which creates a `blocks` edge from the predecessor; `parent_task_id` creates a `parent_child` edge parent -> new task. Both must already exist and are resolved from a full id OR an unambiguous >= 6-character prefix. Lens writes the project under BOTH conventions (metadata.project and the project tag, §5B.1) and carries `metadata.lens_request_id` for its own best-effort de-duplication: create mints a new id and inserts with NO uniqueness on any metadata key, so the key is a Lens-side lookup, never an upstream idempotency guarantee (T3 D10).

observed_divergences: `ambiguous_id_prefix` carries `candidates` BESIDE the message, which is the field Lens's coded tool error dropped until T3-W3 (it kept only `code` and `message`) and the reason it now carries the whole envelope. `depends_on` / `parent_task_id` come back as the RESOLVED full ids and are absent when the request supplied none (the `no_links` variant). The `candidates` SHAPE is the one element here not stated by the live tool surface — the input schemas and the return descriptions are, and were re-dumped into `_tools_snapshot.json` in this slice — so a list of full task ids is what the operator's `make contracts-verify` run should look at hardest.
